entries.content: The root cause was that mypy only marked code after an expression as unreachable when a *call* directly returned a bare `NoReturn` (in `visit_call_expr`), but `visit_await_expr` never inspected the type produced by unwrapping the awaited value — so `await gather(no_return(), no_return())`, whose awaited result type contains uninhabited components (`Tuple[NoReturn, NoReturn]` nested in the awaitable), left the rest of the `NoReturn` coroutine "reachable" and triggered the bogus "Implicit return in function which does not return" error. The fix updates `visit_await_expr` in `mypy/checkexpr.py` to call `self.chk.binder.unreachable()` when the awaited result type has an uninhabited component (via the existing `has_uninhabited_component` query, which handles plain `NoReturn`, tuples, and similar composite types), while preserving the existing "ambiguous inference" exemption for a bare ambiguous `UninhabitedType`. Verified with the issue repro, additional edge cases (variables holding awaitables, `Coroutine[Any, Any, NoReturn]`, normal awaits remaining reachable), and the full `testcheck` plus async `testpythoneval` suites pass.
